target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `main-session-recovery-state.ts` is the single pure interpreter for recovery state, lifecycle fences, foreground claims, reservations, tombstones, and health/reset transitions.
- `main-session-recovery-store.ts` commits those transitions atomically through the session accessor writer lock; callers submit closed domain commands instead of mutating recovery fields.
- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway performs a non-consuming validation during its normal session transaction, then atomically admits the exact reservation only at the final acceptance boundary. Abort and foreground-owner races preserve a recoverable interrupted state without leaking run registries.
- Reservation cancellation follows the reservation identity if Gateway canonicalizes a legacy session key during admission.
- Foreground admissions use lifecycle-generation-scoped token sets to fence concurrent recovery scans. Shared ingress claims cover direct agent-command callers as well as Gateway RPC.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

## Evidence

Final reviewed range:

```text
base: 1e0c3e9ee902365dcf9536f83313089c5fc0cf50
head: 5c3ad51f5294c50c497df5b4668df23e535a44da
```

Docker-backed proof used Crabbox's `--provider docker` alias. The actual backend reported `provider=local-container`, lease `cbx_766e2e402160` (`quick-crab`), runtime `docker`, with the host Docker socket disabled. The proof tree matched the local head tree exactly.

- Full changed gate passed in 12m18s: formatting, Plugin SDK baseline, core/core-test and extension/extension-test tsgo, core/extension lint, database-first guard, import-cycle checks, and all other selected lanes.
- Final incremental proof after `9b92eb839c4`: Gateway recovery filter passed 12 tests (482 skipped), core/core-test tsgo passed, targeted format/lint passed, and the full build passed in 5m03s.
- Exact-head CI exposed a Doctor owner mismatch: tombstones were discovered in legacy JSON but repaired through the canonical SQLite accessor. `5c3ad51f529` moves main-recovery discovery and tests to the canonical accessor; the full Doctor file passed 36/36, target format/lint and `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused recovery proof passed: recovery state 13 tests, session store 56, reply admission 38, and recovery store 11.
- Earlier broad affected-surface proof remains useful: `cbx_3ade43a18ecb` passed 8 Vitest shards / 1454 tests plus extension and extension-test tsgo.
- Public-release hygiene passed: gitleaks scanned the 43-commit range with no leaks, and no local absolute paths were present in the diff.

Final Auto Review used the default Codex engine, not Claude. The branch diff exceeded the reviewer's 180 KB input limit, so it was reviewed as two logical bundles. One actionable finding was accepted and fixed in `9b92eb839c4`: ingress preparation rejection now restores the interrupted recovery state. The remaining findings were rejected after checking the Gateway final-acceptance boundary and SQLite transaction contract; no accepted/actionable finding remains. A final default-Codex local review of the two-file Doctor follow-up was clean with no findings.

Docs proof passed formatting, Markdown lint, MDX validation, i18n glossary validation, and 5811 internal links with zero broken links. `docs:map:check` still reports the known unrelated `docs/docs_map.md` baseline drift; this PR changes only the Doctor page body and does not change its frontmatter or map inputs.

Exact-head CI passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29185290915

The prior real Telegram Desktop behavior proof remains useful scenario coverage:

- Telegram workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
- Artifact bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
- Manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The Telegram baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate quarantined the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume.
